title: Largest Number With K Swaps and Boolean Parenthesization
statement:
This online assessment had two classic problems. Solve both for the given input and print one answer per line.

**Task 1: Largest number with at most K swaps.** You are given a positive integer as a string of digits `s` (no leading zero) and an integer `k`. In one swap you may pick any two positions of `s` and exchange their digits. Perform **at most** `k` swaps (possibly fewer, possibly none) to make the number as large as possible, and report that largest number as a digit string.

**Task 2: Boolean parenthesization.** You are given a boolean expression `expr` made of the operands `T` (true) and `F` (false) joined by the binary operators `&` (and), `|` (or) and `^` (xor), strictly alternating: operand, operator, operand, ..., operand. Count the number of ways to fully parenthesize the expression so that it evaluates to **true**. Two parenthesizations are different if they group the operators in a different order of evaluation. Print the count modulo `1000000007`.

A single operand has exactly one parenthesization (itself).
inputFormat: A single line (or whitespace-separated tokens) with three values: the digit string `s`, the integer `k`, and the expression `expr` (no spaces).
outputFormat: Print two lines. Line 1: the largest number obtainable from `s` with at most `k` swaps. Line 2: the number of parenthesizations of `expr` that evaluate to true, modulo `1000000007`.
constraints: 1 ≤ length of s ≤ 15; s has no leading zero
1 ≤ number of operands in expr ≤ 200 (so the length of expr is at most 399)

examples.explanation: Task 1: with one swap the best move is to put the largest digit 4 in front by swapping it with the 1, giving 4231. Task 2: `(T^F)&F` = `T&F` = false, while `T^(F&F)` = `T^F` = true, so exactly 1 parenthesization is true.

Task 1: the first swap brings a 9 to the front (7599 becomes 9579), the second swaps the 5 with the last 9 (9975). Task 2: the five parenthesizations evaluate as (T|(F^(T&T))) true, (T|((F^T)&T)) true, ((T|F)^(T&T)) false, ((T|(F^T))&T) true, (((T|F)^T)&T) false: 3 are true.
Task 1: the digits are already in descending order, so the number cannot be improved. Task 2: the expression is the single operand `F`, which is false, so there are 0 true parenthesizations.

complexity.time: Task 1: backtracking with pruning over at most k swaps; Task 2: O(m^3) interval DP for m operands

hints: Task 1: process positions left to right. At position i the best you can do is to bring in the largest digit that appears later; if several positions hold that digit, you must try each of them.
Task 1: only spend a swap when the largest later digit is strictly bigger than the digit at i, and stop recursing when no swaps remain. Remember the best string seen so far.

Task 2: let T[i][j] and F[i][j] be the number of ways the operands i..j can evaluate to true and to false. Split at every operator between them and combine the counts of the left and right parts according to &, | or ^.
